excerpt: Interactive map of Caleb's story: the spies sent from Kadesh, Hebron and the sons of Anak, and the hill country Caleb claimed at 85 (Numbers 13–14; Joshua 14–15).
Map of Shechem in Dinah's story (Genesis 34), the ancient city at Tell Balata beside modern Nablus, with notes on what the evidence can and cannot locate.
Map of Moab in Balaam's story (Numbers 22–24): the Moabite highlands above Israel's camp on the plains east of the Jordan, across from Jericho.
Map of Jael's story in Judges 4–5: Heber's camp near Kedesh, the battle at Mount Tabor and the Kishon, and why her tent can't be placed exactly.
Map of Jerusalem in Nicodemus's story. All three of his appearances in John take place in the city during Jesus's ministry and death.
Map of Jerusalem in Athaliah's story: her rule, the hidden boy king Joash, and the confrontation that ended her reign (2 Kings 11; 2 Chronicles 22–23).
Map of Rachel's story from Harran to the road near Ephrath (Bethlehem) in Genesis, marking endpoints the text names rather than an unrecorded route.
Map of Jerusalem in Bathsheba's story, with Rabbah, the Ammonite capital near modern Amman where Uriah died (2 Samuel 11–12; 1 Kings 1–2).
Map of Absalom's story: born in Hebron, living in Jerusalem, and launching his claim to David's throne from Hebron (2 Samuel 13–18).
Map of Naomi's journey between Bethlehem and Moab in the Book of Ruth. The Moabite marker is regional because Ruth names no town or route.
Map of James son of Zebedee's story, from his call by the Sea of Galilee to his death in Jerusalem under Herod Agrippa I (Mark 1; Acts 12).
Map of Ezra's journey from Babylon to Jerusalem. The book gives a four-month span but no route, so the map marks endpoints (Ezra 7–10; Nehemiah 8).
Map of the Sea of Galilee in Andrew's story: his home town of Bethsaida and the lake region where he worked, with notes on debated sites.
Map of Hagar's story in Genesis 16 and 21: the road to Shur, Beer Lahai Roi, the Desert of Beersheba and Paran, south of Canaan.
Map of Jerusalem in Joab's story, the center of David's rule and of Joab's military command, though his campaigns ranged far beyond the city.
Map of Achan's story in Joshua 6–7, connecting captured Jericho with Israel's failed attack on Ai in the central hill country.
Map of Michal's story, centered on Gibeah, her father Saul's seat, and Jerusalem, King David's capital (1 and 2 Samuel).
Map of Jericho in Zacchaeus's story (Luke 19), in the Jordan Valley northeast of Jerusalem, where Jesus stopped on his way to the city.
Map of Uriah's story: summoned to Jerusalem while Israel's army besieged Rabbah, the Ammonite capital near modern Amman (2 Samuel 11).
A broad map of the ancient Near East for Abel's story. Genesis doesn't name where Abel lived, so this map deliberately places no marker for him.
Map of Naaman's story (2 Kings 5): from the Aramean capital region around Damascus to Israel and the Jordan River, where he washed.
Map of Miriam's story, from the Nile in Egypt through Israel's wilderness journey, with notes on why the Exodus routes remain disputed.
Map of Simon of Cyrene's story: from Cyrene, a Greek-speaking city in today's Libya, to Jerusalem, where he carried Jesus's cross.
Map of Ahab's story: Samaria, his capital, and his royal residence at Jezreel in the northern kingdom of Israel (1 Kings 16–22).
Map of Nob in Doeg's story (1 Samuel 21–22), the priestly town near Jerusalem where David received bread and Goliath's sword. Its site is unconfirmed.
Map of Midian in Zipporah's story, the region east of the Gulf of Aqaba in northwestern Arabia where Moses lived with her family (Exodus 2, 4 and 18).
Map of Shechem in Abimelech's story (Judges 9), the city at Tell Balata near Nablus whose people backed his rise to power.
Map of Jerusalem's temple site in Zechariah's story, where the prophet encouraged rebuilding after the exile. It marks the wider compound only.
Map of Hebron in Sarah's story, near Mamre where Abraham and Sarah camped, about 19 miles south of Jerusalem in today's West Bank.
Map of Jerusalem's temple in Anna's story (Luke 2), where the prophetess met the infant Jesus, marking the Temple Mount compound in today's Old City.
Map of Capernaum in Matthew's story, the village on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee where Jesus called him from his tax booth.
Map of the Nile Delta in Jochebed's story (Exodus 2), the region of northern Egypt where Moses' mother hid him. Her home is not identified.
Map of Caesarea in Cornelius's story (Acts 10), the Roman port on Israel's Mediterranean coast about 30 miles north of Tel Aviv.
Map of Elizabeth's story in Luke 1: the hill country of Judea and Ein Karem, traditionally linked to Mary's visit, about five miles from Jerusalem.
Map of the hill country of Ephraim in Micah's story (Judges 17–18), the central highlands north of Jerusalem, using Shechem as a landmark.
Map of Shechem in Rehoboam's story (1 Kings 12), where the assembly that split the kingdom met, at Tell Balata near Nablus.
Map of Babylon in Manasseh's story (2 Chronicles 33), whose ruins lie in modern Iraq about 53 miles south of Baghdad.
Map of Carmel in Nabal's story (1 Samuel 25), the southern Judean village of al-Karmil, about eight miles south-southeast of Hebron.
Map of Jerusalem in Nathan's story, the city where the prophet advised and confronted King David (2 Samuel 7; 12).
Map of Jerusalem in Ahithophel's story, the city David fled and Absalom entered during the rebellion that Ahithophel advised (2 Samuel 15–17).
Where was the land of Uz? A map and guide to the setting of the Book of Job, weighing the Edom and southern Syria (Hauran) proposals.
